traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.45, 0.4, 0.35], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: usual 8-20 m, the tallest about 25 m; Reiche (1896) calls it a modest shrub in central Chile and a tall, stout tree in the south.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 202, Drimys winteri: leaves elliptic to oblanceolate, dark green above and whitish below; Reiche (1896, p. 26-27) has them obovate or lanceolate, short-stalked and leathery, the outline between those.

traits.inflorescence.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26-27, Drimys Winteri: flowers alone in the upper leaf axils or in stalked umbels, or both on one plant (Simpson p. 202: an umbel-like cyme).

traits.fruit_type.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26-27, Drimys Winteri: berries blackish.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26-27, Drimys Winteri: berries blackish. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: Reiche (1896) has it flowering from May in the north to September at Valdivia.

generator.params.note: Pacific madrone's crown values, changed by hand: one straight trunk with ascending branches into a narrow crown. Not fitted to measurements. spur_leaf is the leaf card the angiosperm rule gives leaf_size, 1.5 times the flora's mean blade, so short-shoot leaves are drawn the same size. Its crown's width is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured width over height of open-grown trees of its lineage (crown_spread, USDA Urban Tree Database) since 2026-10-23, in place of a hand-set crown_radius. Its crown's base is the broadleaf trees' rule from the measured share of the tree's height below its crown (crown_base_share, USDA Urban Tree Database), and its stem divides only where its flora or photographs say its leader is lost or that it stands on several stems, since 2026-10-24, in place of hand-set crown_base and fork values.

allometry.note: 15 m at 40 years in the open, within the model estimate's usual 8-20 m. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Reiche (1896) and Simpson: pale grey bark and red young twigs; glossy leaves, whitish below.
